description: Writes a block from textual SCL source and (optionally) compiles it. Gd6: use THIS for TEXTUAL language (SCL/STL); for graphical (LAD/FBD/GRAPH) use tia_import_xml. With compile:true, the raw compile DTO is nested under 'compile' (same as tia_compile's response), and 'located[]' plus a nextHint are merged at the TOP LEVEL of the result — same place tia_compile puts them — when the compile regenerated blocks, e.g. an instance DB after an FB interface change. `generatedOrUpdated` lists every block the source created or regenerated (app ≥ v1.6.0; older serves list only new ones) — TIA regenerates a block even when the text is identical, so it then needs a compile — and `sourceChanges` gives the per-block change and parts. Stale-write guard: pass the `contentHash` you read (tia_export_block, tia_export_type or tia_type_source) as `expectedContentHash` and the serve checks it BEFORE writing — a mismatch is 409 state_changed and NOTHING is written; a match adds `contentGuard` to the result. `contentHash`, `normalizedSha256` and `sha256` are different hash contracts over different normalizations: never substitute one for another, and pass only the `contentHash` of a fresh read as `expectedContentHash`. It guards exactly ONE object: the code must declare exactly one block or type (else 400 bad_request), and a hash for an object that does not exist (any more) is refused as state_changed — omit it to create. The guard never compiles: an existing block that is not consistent is refused with 409 inconsistent (compile, re-read with tia_export_block, retry), and an existing object whose current export is not well-formed XML cannot be hashed and is refused with 409 unverifiable (NOTHING is written; repair it, or omit expectedContentHash to write without the guard). Needs an app with the guard: an older serve ignores the field and the result says the write was NOT guarded. dryRun never verifies it. Regenerating a block replaces its project object: V21 drops its VCI mapping (measured), so a mapped block leaves tia_vci_status and must be exported again (tia_vci_export). Maps to POST /plcs/{plc}/source. M-off. Long operation: may answer status:"running" + jobId — then call tia_job_status.

dryRun.description: Gd11: plan-without-applying — validates the guards and describes the action WITHOUT mutating the project

expectedContentHash.description: Stale-write guard (optional): the `contentHash` of the object as you last read it (tia_export_block, tia_export_type or tia_type_source; 64 hex characters). `contentHash`, `normalizedSha256` and `sha256` are different hash contracts over different normalizations: never substitute one for another, and pass only the `contentHash` of a fresh read as `expectedContentHash`. The serve compares it with the object's CURRENT hash inside the same operation, BEFORE writing, and refuses with 409 state_changed (nothing written) when it differs; a match is confirmed by `contentGuard` in the result. It guards exactly ONE object per write (the source must declare exactly one block or type, else 400 bad_request). A hash for an object that does not exist (any more) is refused as state_changed, so omit it when creating. The guard never compiles: an existing object that is not consistent is refused with 409 inconsistent and nothing written (compile, re-read with tia_export_block / tia_export_type, retry); one whose current export is not well-formed XML cannot be hashed and is refused with 409 unverifiable (nothing written; repair it, or omit expectedContentHash to write without the guard). Needs an app with the guard. dryRun does NOT verify it: the plan only shows it.
